newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel says 4 youngest hostage-takers gave up.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel says 4 youngest hostage-takers gave up.

text.p: The four youngest Tupac Amaru rebels inside the Japanese ambassador's home tried to surrender before being killed during the Peruvian security forces' hostage rescue Tuesday, a rebel said.

"They were the four youngest. They were in a room on their own. They gave up out of fear," the Tupac Amaru Revolutiuonary Movement (MRTA) rebel, who asked to remain anonymous but identified himself using a codename, told Reuters.
The MRTA member claimed he heard the hostage-takers' surrender while monitoring an open, short-wave radio communication which the rebels had with their comrades in Lima.
The attack on the mined and booby-trapped compound left one hostage, two officers and all 14 of the jungle-trained, mainly teenage rebels dead.
The operation to rescue 72 VIPs held under the gun for 126 days took place while MRTA rebels held a soccer match inside the residence, according to freed Bolivian Ambassador Jorge Gumucio.
The MRTA's international spokesman, Isaac Velazco, could not confirm some rebels tried to give themselves up but said the ski-masked security forces "assassinated" the rebel hostage-takers.
